topic: Trader-centric Celnet FX-options client SDK and wire API: how desks actually work, competitor API critique, and a concrete gRPC/WS + Rust SDK surface with real-like workflow integration tests
summary: FX-options desks operate around five workflow loops the current Celnet edge does not yet model: (1) RFQ (discrete request -> competing quotes -> accept/last-look -> booking) and RFS (subscribe-once, continuous two-way streaming prices/Greeks for a *defined structure*, with a tradable window of typically up to ~5 minutes); (2) vol-surface marking/blotter (calibrate at the main mark, re-mark intraday on material moves and central-bank events, broker ATM/25d&10d RR/BF quotes -> arb-free smile, with traders wanting to see *why* each point is what it is); (3) structured/exotic booking (multi-leg strategies: risk reversal, strangle, straddle, seagull; and path-dependent structures: barriers, digitals, one-touch/DNT, TARFs, accumulators/pivot — booked as a single contract with legs/schedules, often zero-premium-solved); (4) risk/scenario/what-if (run spot/vol/rate shocks on every pricing update, multi-factor grids, tiered limits); (5) position & P&L with risk-factor attribution (delta/gamma/vega/theta/vanna/volga decomposition between marks). The current Celnet edge (PricingEdge gRPC: unary PriceVanilla/SurfaceVol/PriceBarrier/Readiness; WS RfsServer broadcasting a single hard-coded reference-strike PriceUpdate to all subscribers) is a solid latency/lifecycle skeleton but is NOT yet trader-shaped: RFS is a fixed broadcast not a per-subscriber structure subscription; there is no RFQ/quote/accept lifecycle, no idempotent request/quote IDs beyond an echoed uint64, no strategy/multi-leg or structured-product instrument, no surface-mark or scenario or position/P&L surface, no subscribe/snapshot+delta+resync semantics, and the WS stream is JSON-only with no typed contract. Competitor critique: every incumbent (SynOption, Fenics FMD/kACE, Bloomberg OVML/BVOL/MARS, 360T, Digital Vega Medusa) is RFQ/seconds-scale, closed-analytics, FIX-or-terminal oriented with no customer-extensible model SDK and no microsecond streaming-quote contract — that seam is exactly what a modern typed gRPC+WS contract plus a typed Rust client SDK can win. Recommendation: define a single current Celnet wire contract (one .proto family) with an Instrument model (vanilla | strategy-of-legs | barrier | digital | touch | tarf | accumulator), an RFQ lifecycle (QuoteRequest/Quote/QuoteAccept/QuoteReject/Execution with client-supplied idempotency keys), an RFS bidi stream keyed on a client SubscriptionId carrying a snapshot + sequenced deltas + heartbeat + explicit Resync, a surface read/mark/scenario service, and a position/P&L service; and a typed async Rust client SDK (celnet-client) that wraps these as ergonomic futures/streams with reconnect+resync built in. Drive and critique the API with ~12 real-like end-to-end workflow integration tests that exercise each loop against the live edge.
key_findings: RFS (request-for-stream) is the dominant electronic FX-options price-distribution model and is structurally different from Celnet's current WS broadcast: a client subscribes to a SPECIFIC structure (pair, expiry, strike or delta, side(s), notional, strategy legs) and receives continuous two-way (bid/offer) prices+Greeks streamed for a bounded tradable window (Digital Vega Medusa streams competing RFS prices for up to ~5 minutes and recalculates best bid/offer live; 360T Bridge is a 'by traders, for traders' RFS GUI). Celnet's RfsServer instead prices ONE hard-coded reference strike and fans the identical PriceUpdate to every subscriber — there is no per-subscriber instrument, no two-way price, no notional, no quote validity/expiry.

RFQ is a discrete request/response lifecycle the edge has no model for: in FIX terms QuoteRequest(35=R) -> Quote(35=S) (two-way when side/qty omitted) -> client accepts -> Execution; multi-leg strategies (risk reversal, strangle, straddle, seagull) are quoted as one request via NoLegs/strategy definition (FIX Appendix E multileg; SecurityDefinition 35=c to define a strategy). Desks expect a stable QuoteID per quote, a ClOrdID/idempotency key per request, last-look/quote-expiry, and partial/multi-dealer aggregation. Celnet's only correlation is an echoed uint64 request_id with no quote object, no accept path, no expiry, no idempotency-on-retry guarantee.

Vol-surface marking is a first-class trader workflow, not just a read: traders calibrate the surface at the main mark (close) and re-mark intraday on material spot moves and central-bank announcements, working in broker conventions (ATM, 25-delta and 10-delta RR & BF per tenor) and two-curve (dom/for) forward construction, and they want transparency into why each smile point is what it is. Celnet exposes only SurfaceVol(strike,tenor)->vol read; there is no mark/override/recalibrate path, no broker-quote-set ingest+arb-repair surface object on the wire, no per-tenor smile read (delta axis), no surface snapshot/version stream — yet celnet-surface already builds the arb-free surface internally, so this is an exposure gap, not a math gap.

Structured/exotic booking needs an instrument model the wire lacks: TARFs and accumulators/pivot are a SERIES of legs/fixings with a target-redemption (knock-out on cumulative gain) and gearing/multiplier, usually zero-upfront (premium-solved); barriers/digitals/touches carry barrier level(s), rebate, monitoring style. The edge has only PriceBarrier (single barrier, single leg) and PriceVanilla; there is no strategy-of-legs message, no fixing schedule, no target/gearing, no solve-for-strike/premium-to-zero request, and no booking/term-sheet result. celnet-exotics already prices these — again an exposure gap.

Risk/scenario/what-if is run on every pricing update with shock grids (e.g. spot -20%, ATM vol +100%, multi-factor spot+rate shocks) under tiered loss limits, and P&L attribution decomposes the move between marks into delta/gamma/vega/theta/vanna/volga risk-factor contributions. Celnet returns the 14-Greek set on a single point but has no scenario/shock-grid request, no portfolio/position aggregation, and no P&L-attribution service — these are absent from the wire entirely.

Programmatic-API expectations the edge half-meets: streaming needs snapshot-then-delta with a monotonic sequence, heartbeats, explicit gap detection AND a server-assisted RESYNC (not just 'continue from next update' on lag), idempotent request keys so a client retry after a timeout cannot double-book, subscription management (subscribe/modify/unsubscribe with a client SubscriptionId), and backpressure that is per-subscriber (Celnet's single broadcast::channel(256) lags slow consumers globally and silently skips — acceptable for indicative streaming but unsafe as the only mechanism for tradable quotes). Celnet has sequence + lag-resync + heartbeat-via-ws-ping + readiness/drain — a good base — but no snapshot, no server resync RPC, no idempotency contract, no typed WS schema (JSON only).

SynOption critique: MAS-regulated multi-bank RFQ venue (Optimus) with broad product coverage (vanillas, multi-leg, digitals/one-touch/DNT/barriers, TARF/pivot/accumulators) and FIX STP, but built for human RFQ (seconds-scale, indicative), publishes NO latency/throughput numbers, ships closed Orion 'risk libraries' with only spread/skew knobs (no customer-extensible quant SDK), exposes only FIX+UI+thin STP with no public REST/gRPC/WebSocket developer portal or docs, and is SaaS/venue-locked (no on-prem/in-process embedding). API gap = no modern typed streaming contract, no programmable models.

Fenics critique: FMD FXO 2.0 is best-in-class DATA (300+ pairs + 27 metals, tradable-not-consensus ATM/25d&10d RR/BF wing quotes) but it is a data feed, not an interactive pricing API — repricing/what-if/Greeks are the consumer's problem, conventions (spot vs fwd delta, premium-adj) and smile-interpolation/no-arb method are under-documented, distribution leans on snapshot/intraday/FTP/SFTP + LSEG redistribution (not push-native sub-second), and analytics (kACE) is a separately-licensed heavyweight Excel/OMS desktop tool on dated FIX 4.4. API gap = no streaming push, no documented convention contract, no callable arb-free surface object.

Bloomberg critique: OVML structures/prices vanillas+strategies with selectable vol source (BVOL/LIVE/Custom); BVOL gives trusted real-time surfaces on 200+ pairs (bid/ask/timestamp, moneyness/delta/tenor points) reachable via BLPAPI/SAPI tickers; MARS adds cross-asset risk+scenario with a Python API. But it is a closed seat-priced terminal/feed (BLPAPI ticker-string pattern, B-PIPE/SAPI feed tax), has NO customer-extensible model SDK (you consume Bloomberg's models), and is not an embeddable in-colo microsecond pricing service. API gap = ticker/feed-oriented not message/streaming-quote-oriented, no programmable payoffs.

360T (Bridge RFS GUI, EMS supporting RFQ/RFS/ESP/algos) and Digital Vega Medusa (FIX-connected to major banks, streamed pricing 60+ pairs in standard structures, RFQ to up to 5 providers, 4 simultaneous requests, live best-bid/offer recompute, automated TWAP/expiry, pre-trade TCA) are strong WORKFLOW/venue networks but outsource real pricing to bank LPs and standard models — they are not a differentiated quant engine with an open model SDK. API gap = venue/aggregation FIX surface, not an extensible pricing/risk contract.
recommendations: Define ONE current Celnet wire contract as a small .proto family (no version field, per guardrail 9): celnet.instrument (the Instrument model), celnet.quote (RFQ lifecycle), celnet.stream (RFS), celnet.surface (read/mark/scenario), celnet.position (position+P&L). Keep message bodies mirroring celnet-types/celnet-proto one-to-one as edge.proto already does, and keep identifiers purpose-named/vendor-neutral (VanillaInputs not GkInputs).

Introduce a unified Instrument oneof so every workflow speaks one vocabulary: Instrument = { Vanilla | Strategy(repeated Leg with ratio/side) | Barrier | Digital | Touch(one-touch/no-touch/DNT) | Tarf(legs + fixing schedule + target + gearing) | Accumulator(schedule + KO + gearing) }. Add a Quantity (notional + which leg-ccy) and a Solve directive (solve strike or premium so a leg/structure is zero-cost). This exposes celnet-vanilla/celnet-exotics that already price these — closing the exposure gaps in findings 4.

Add an RFQ lifecycle service: rpc RequestQuote(QuoteRequest) returns (Quote); rpc AcceptQuote(QuoteAccept) returns (Execution); plus QuoteReject. QuoteRequest carries a client-supplied idempotency_key (string/UUID) and Instrument + side(s) (omit side => two-way bid/offer like FIX) + quantity; Quote carries a server quote_id, two-way price (bid/offer premium in chosen PremiumStyle), full Greeks, a valid_until timestamp (quote expiry/last-look), and the resolved convention. Idempotency: same key returns the same quote_id/execution, never double-books on retry.

Replace the single-broadcast RFS with a bidirectional stream keyed on a client SubscriptionId: rpc Stream(stream ClientStreamMsg) returns (stream ServerStreamMsg). ClientStreamMsg = { Subscribe(SubscriptionId, Instrument, two-way, throttle_hint) | Modify | Unsubscribe | Resync(SubscriptionId, last_seq) | Heartbeat }. ServerStreamMsg = { Snapshot(SubscriptionId, seq, two-way price+Greeks+vol) | Delta(seq, changed fields) | Heartbeat(seq) | Lagged(resync_required) | StreamEnd(reason) }. Per-subscription sequence + snapshot+delta + server-assisted Resync fixes finding 6; keep the existing draining/readiness behavior to refuse new subscriptions while blue-green-draining.

Expose the surface as a workflow, not just a point read: rpc GetSmile(pair,tenor) returns (Smile on a delta axis with ATM/25d&10d RR/BF and the arb-repair status); rpc MarkSurface(pair, broker quote set, conventions) returns (calibrated surface version id) for the marking/blotter loop; rpc StreamSurface(pair) for push re-marks on material moves; and carry an explicit conventions block (DeltaConvention x PremiumStyle x AtmConvention x DayCount x Cut) on every surface message so the 'show me why' transparency in finding 3 is on the wire (a Celnet differentiator vs Fenics/Bloomberg opacity).

Add risk/scenario and position/P&L services: rpc Scenario(Instrument or PortfolioRef, ShockGrid) returns (repeated ScenarioPoint{shock, price, Greeks}) where ShockGrid = axes of spot/vol/rate shocks (absolute or relative) — implements the what-if grids of finding 5; rpc GetPosition(book) returns (aggregated Greeks + positions); rpc AttributePnl(book, from_mark, to_mark) returns (per-risk-factor decomposition: delta/gamma/vega/theta/vanna/volga + residual). These can compose the existing engine without new math.

Ship a typed async Rust client SDK crate `celnet-client` over tonic+tokio: a `CelnetClient::connect(endpoint)`; ergonomic methods `price(Instrument) -> Greeks`, `request_quote(QuoteRequest) -> Quote`, `accept(&Quote) -> Execution`; an `rfs.subscribe(Instrument) -> impl Stream<Item = PriceTick>` that internally manages SubscriptionId, applies snapshot+deltas into a current two-way state, auto-heartbeats, and on disconnect reconnects and Resyncs from last_seq transparently; `surface.mark(...)`, `surface.smile(...)`; `scenario(...)`, `position(...)`, `attribute_pnl(...)`. Idempotency keys auto-generated (overridable), reconnect/backoff built in. Re-export the proto types so callers never touch raw tonic.

Keep the WS edge as the browser/light-client mirror of the SAME contract but make it typed: serialize the identical stream messages (Snapshot/Delta/Heartbeat/Lagged) as a tagged JSON enum (serde internally-tagged), not a single flat PriceUpdate, so the GUI consumes the same semantics (snapshot+delta+resync) as gRPC. Document that gRPC bidi is the primary low-latency path and WS is the firewall-friendly mirror — one contract, two transports.

Generate observability and the latency proof alongside: per-RPC and per-subscription latency histograms (ties to pending task #18) and a published RFS quote-to-tick latency number — this converts the 'microsecond' claim into the evidence finding-1/competitor-critique says incumbents lack. Wire the histograms off the hot path (sampling/atomic counters) per guardrail 6.

Drive and critique the design with ~12 real-like end-to-end workflow integration tests in celnet-server/tests (and celnet-client examples) that each run against a live edge and assert the trader semantics; let failures/ergonomic friction in these tests force contract changes BEFORE freezing (the 'evolve API by use' intent of task #17). Treat any test that needs a workaround as an API-design defect to fix in the proto, not in the test.
risks: Scope/idempotency correctness: an RFQ accept path plus idempotency keys touches booking semantics; a weak idempotency store (or one that is not durable across the blue-green cutover) can double-book on retry during an upgrade. Must specify idempotency-key lifetime, dedupe store, and behavior across drain/cutover, or restrict v1 to indicative-only quotes with explicit 'not for STP' marking.

Interface-freeze blast radius (guardrail 9/10): this is a large addition to the single current contract; per INTERFACES.md changing it means editing the proto + every dependent in one change and re-indexing the memory graph. The Instrument oneof in particular will ripple into celnet-vanilla/exotics call sites — sequence it as a deliberate coordinated interface change, not piecemeal.

Per-subscriber streaming cost vs the current single-broadcast design: moving from one broadcast::channel to per-subscription pricing+sequencing increases work per tick and per connection; at IB-portfolio/HFT fan-out (guardrail 6) this needs a fan-out strategy (shared pricing for identical instruments, throttle hints, conflation of deltas) or it will not scale — design the subscription registry for instrument-dedup from day one.

Two-way / last-look / quote-expiry semantics are easy to get subtly wrong (stale quote accepted after valid_until, or bid/offer skew applied inconsistently with PremiumStyle); these are exactly the convention traps the competitive doc says Celnet wins on, so they must be tested against worked examples, not merely asserted plausible (guardrail 5).

TARF/accumulator wire model is genuinely complex (fixing schedules, target/gearing, KO accounting, zero-premium solve); an under-specified Tarf/Accumulator message risks becoming a placeholder, which violates the no-mocks guardrail — either model the schedule/target fully or narrow v1 to the structures already fully priced in celnet-exotics and add the rest as a deliberate later coordinated change.

WS JSON tagged-enum mirror can drift from the gRPC proto if hand-maintained; without a single source of truth (generate the JSON schema from the proto types) the 'one contract, two transports' claim breaks — enforce that both serialize the same Rust types.

Web research is positioning-grade for competitor internals: SynOption/Fenics/360T/Digital Vega publish little public API detail, so several critique points are inferred from product descriptions (as the existing COMPETITIVE-ANALYSIS.md already flags). Treat competitor API specifics as directional, not vendor-confirmed.

topic: Celnet observability zero hot path cost
summary: The pinned zero alloc pricing core only bumps relaxed CachePadded atomics and pushes POD records to a bounded SPSC ring while a drain thread and the tokio edge own tracing OTLP metrics and HdrHistogram.
key_findings: The pinned core only bumps relaxed CachePadded atomics and pushes a POD record to an SPSC ring
Deferred formatting is far cheaper than inline formatted logging on the hot path
tracing and tracing subscriber stay on the edge while OTel Rust metrics is stable but tracing is pre release
HdrHistogram with correction avoids coordinated omission and USDT probes are free when disabled
recommendations: Create a celnet observe crate holding POD records the ring the drain thread tracing OTLP HdrHistogram and USDT
Instrument the core with only relaxed counters and one POD push per request dropping on a full ring
Add CI gates for zero allocation with telemetry on and a benchmark latency budget
risks: Coordinated omission hides tail latency unless correction and end to end measurement are used
One stray tracing format or allocation in the core breaks the zero allocation guarantee
Telemetry must drop while audit must never drop so they need separate rings and drains

topic: Scaling Celnet — distributed-systems architecture and partitioning model for IB-sized FX-options pricing/streaming at microsecond latencies (best practices, May 2026)
summary: For an FX-options pricing/streaming platform like Celnet, the right architecture is a hybrid: keep the latency-critical work on a fat, NUMA-pinned, thread-per-core single node and only go distributed for capacity, fault-tolerance, and fan-out — never to make a single price faster. The single-thread/single-node ceiling is extremely high (LMAX's business-logic processor handles ~6M events/s on one thread; Celnet already targets ≥1M price updates/s/core and p50 ≤2µs vanilla pricing on a pinned core), so distribution must be designed to NOT cross the hot path. The recommended shape: (1) a shard = one pinned engine instance owning a disjoint set of (currency-pair × book/tenant) partitions, assigned by rendezvous (HRW) hashing so adding/removing shards moves minimal state; (2) market-data (arb-free surface + curves) is event-sourced and fanned out via an Aeron-style replicated log to per-shard local replicas, each pricer reading a lock-free arc-swap snapshot so prices are computed against a node-local, near-zero-staleness copy with no cross-node read on the path; (3) counterparty streaming uses an in-process LMAX-disruptor SPMC ring (the model Celnet already mirrors with its in-proc distributor) at the core, with SO_REUSEPORT sharded accept + conflation/last-value-cache at the edge, and kernel-bypass (DPDK or io_uring/XDP) only where the wire budget demands it; (4) consistency/failover via Raft-replicated event log (Aeron Cluster pattern) giving deterministic replay, hot-standby shards, and blue-green/SO_REUSEPORT handoff Celnet already specifies. Net: Celnet should stay single-node per shard for pricing and quoting, and be distributed only at the granularity of shards (capacity + HA) and the market-data/event log (consistency + replay). Build the shard router, HRW partitioner, replicated MD log, and per-shard surface snapshot first; defer cross-node DPDK multicast and a global RDMA fabric until a single shard's edge fan-out is provably the bottleneck.
key_findings: Single-node ceiling is very high: LMAX's business-logic processor sustains ~6M events/s on ONE thread by keeping caches warm and avoiding main-memory/cross-core traffic; the Disruptor pipeline shows ~3 orders of magnitude lower mean latency and ~8x throughput vs queue-based designs. Rule of thumb from that body of work: if vertical (scale-up + mechanical sympathy) solves it, do NOT scale out. Distribution adds network hops (kernel stack ~20-50µs; even DPDK userspace ~7µs) that dwarf Celnet's p50 ≤2µs vanilla budget — so any cross-node hop on the hot path is disqualifying.

Celnet's own NFRs already assume single-node mechanical sympathy: p50 ≤2µs / p99 ≤10µs vanilla on a pinned core, ≥1M updates/s/core via thread-per-core lock-free fan-out with no cross-core cache traffic, huge pages + mlock + prefault + NUMA-local + IRQ affinity per Rigtorp tuning. This means the hot core must NOT depend on a distributed read for surface/curve data — distribution belongs around it, not inside it.

Partitioning: rendezvous (HRW / highest-random-weight) hashing is now generally preferred over classic consistent hashing for shard assignment — simpler, no token ring to precompute/store, better load balance, minimal reshuffle on node add/remove (used by Kafka, Twitter EventBus). For FX options the natural shard key is (currency-pair) as the primary axis, sub-partitioned by book/tenant where a single hot pair (e.g. EURUSD) exceeds one core; all tenors of a pair stay co-resident on one shard because surface rebuild is per-pair-all-tenors (Celnet targets p99 ≤150µs for that) and must not cross nodes.

Shared state (arb-free surface + curves) is best distributed as an event-sourced, replicated log fanned out to node-LOCAL replicas, not read remotely per price. Industry practice (e.g. SpiderRock) broadcasts live vol surfaces over multicast to execution/risk/pricing consumers. Combined with Celnet's existing arc-swap hot model swap, each pricer should read a lock-free local snapshot (arc-swap) of the latest surface; publisher updates are atomic and readers never block — near-zero staleness, zero cross-node read on the hot path, cache-coherent within the node.

Streaming fan-out: the LMAX Disruptor SPMC ring publishes every event to all consumers from a single producer with no per-consumer queue contention — exactly the in-process distributor pattern Celnet already bridges to (CelNet in-proc disruptor). Mature Rust crates exist (nicholassm/disruptor-rs, the `disruptor` crate, jonhoo/bus broadcast). Note: crossbeam can beat the disruptor for simple SPSC/MPSC because it busy-spins; the disruptor's win is multi-consumer fan-out with consumer interdependency and batch publish — which is the quoting use case.

Edge networking tradeoffs (2025-2026): SO_REUSEPORT (with eBPF SK_REUSEPORT steering) gives sharded accept + graceful handoff with stock kernel — Celnet already uses it for zero-dropped-connection blue-green. DPDK delivers the best raw latency (~7µs userspace floor) and packet rate but costs a dedicated-core/ownership model and ops complexity; io_uring (2025 research: DeferTR+NAPI beats SQPoll; registered buffers help large but slightly hurt small msgs) is the lower-friction middle ground and pairs well with Rust. Recommendation: SO_REUSEPORT + conflation/last-value-cache by default; reach for io_uring/XDP next; reserve full DPDK for the proven extreme tier.

Consistency / failover / replay: Aeron Cluster (Raft consensus, formally proven) is the e-FX-standard pattern — leader appends + replicates to quorum, deterministic replicated state machine rebuild, full-rate archive to disk for real-time-or-later replay, reconnect without message loss, failover bounded by ~2x election timeout. Best-practice guidance: keep the cluster thin (push minimal data through consensus), prefer standby nodes over dynamic membership. This maps cleanly onto Celnet's need for deterministic replay, hot-standby shards, and bit-identical reproducibility.

Backpressure: the disruptor's bounded ring provides natural backpressure; Aeron Archive lets latency-sensitive producers relay without blocking via dynamic flow control. For slow counterparties the correct primitive is conflation (last-value-cache / coalescing) at the edge rather than unbounded buffering — never let a slow subscriber backpressure the pricing core.

Celnet's existing blue-green/hot-upgrade design (SO_REUSEPORT socket handoff + rkyv zero-copy versioned live-state transfer over UDS/shmem + arc-swap hot model swap + SHADOW-style pre-warm) is already the correct per-shard upgrade mechanism; the distributed layer must preserve it per shard and add cross-shard rolling upgrade via the router draining one shard at a time.
recommendations: Adopt a shard-per-pinned-node model. A 'shard' = one Celnet engine process, pinned thread-per-core on a NUMA-local node, owning a disjoint set of partitions. Pricing, surface rebuild, Greeks, and quoting for an owned partition happen entirely in-node with zero cross-node hop on the hot path. Scale capacity by adding shards, not by distributing a single price.

Partition by currency-pair as the primary key using rendezvous (HRW) hashing, sub-sharding hot pairs by book/tenant. Keep ALL tenors of a pair co-resident on one shard (surface rebuild is per-pair-all-tenors). Co-locate a tenant's correlated/cross-pair books on the same shard where risk netting matters; otherwise spread tenants for load balance. HRW gives minimal reshuffle when shards are added/removed.

Build a stateless shard ROUTER/edge tier that maps each request/subscription to its owning shard via the same HRW function and forwards over a fast intra-DC transport. Routers are horizontally scalable and hold no pricing state — only the partition map (versioned, gossiped). This is the only component that scales out 'for free'.

Distribute the arb-free surface + curves via an event-sourced replicated log (Aeron-style/Raft for the authoritative stream), fanned out to a NODE-LOCAL surface cache per shard. Each pricer reads a lock-free arc-swap snapshot; the MD consumer thread swaps in new surfaces atomically. This gives near-zero staleness, no remote read on the hot path, and deterministic replay of the exact surface sequence used for any historical price.

Keep counterparty fan-out as an IN-PROCESS LMAX-disruptor SPMC ring per shard (reuse the existing celnet-distributor bridge / a Rust disruptor crate). One producer (the pricing core) publishes; many consumer threads (one per counterparty session group) read the ring with batch consumption. Apply per-subscriber conflation/last-value-cache so slow counterparties get coalesced latest quotes and can NEVER backpressure the core.

Network edge: default to SO_REUSEPORT sharded accept + eBPF steering (already in Celnet for blue-green) with conflation. Adopt io_uring/XDP as the next performance tier for the WS/gRPC edge. Reserve full DPDK kernel-bypass for a dedicated ultra-low-latency multicast tier only after a single shard's edge fan-out is measured as the bottleneck — record it as an ADR with the io_uring fallback kept first-class (mirrors the CubeCL/wgpu precedent).

Use a thin Raft/Aeron-Cluster-style replicated event log for the authoritative market-data and trade/quote-lifecycle stream to get deterministic replay, hot-standby shards, and bounded failover (~2x election timeout). Keep the consensus path thin — only events that must be ordered/durable go through it; pricing math stays off it. Prefer hot-standby shards over dynamic membership for failover.

Cross-fleet upgrades: extend Celnet's per-shard blue-green (SO_REUSEPORT handoff + rkyv versioned state transfer + arc-swap model swap + SHADOW pre-warm) with a router-driven rolling upgrade — drain/cut over one shard at a time while standbys cover, preserving zero dropped connections and zero in-flight loss across the fleet.

BUILD NOW: HRW partitioner + versioned partition map, stateless shard router, per-shard node-local surface snapshot (arc-swap) fed by a replicated MD log, in-proc disruptor fan-out with conflation, hot-standby shard + deterministic replay from the log. DEFER: full DPDK multicast tier, RDMA cross-node fabric, dynamic cluster membership, and any cross-node distribution of a single option's pricing — until measured single-shard limits justify them.

Add explicit fleet-level SLOs to docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §1.2: per-shard targets (already present) plus cross-shard routing overhead budget, surface-staleness bound (publish-to-local-snapshot lag), failover time bound, and conflation latency for slow subscribers — all measured (HdrHistogram) like the existing NFRs.
risks: Crossing a node boundary on the hot path is fatal to the budget: kernel network stack adds ~20-50µs and even DPDK userspace bottoms out ~7µs, versus Celnet's p50 ≤2µs vanilla target. Any design that reads the surface remotely or routes a single price through the cluster blows the SLA. Mitigation: distribution only around shards and via node-local snapshots, never inside the pricing call.

Hot-pair skew: a few pairs (EURUSD, USDJPY, GBPUSD) can dominate volume and overwhelm a single shard, defeating uniform HRW balance. Mitigation: sub-shard hot pairs by book/tenant or strike/tenor band, and support manual pin/override of the partition map for known-hot pairs; monitor per-shard load and rebalance.

Surface co-residency vs risk netting tension: partitioning by pair maximizes pricing locality but can split a tenant's cross-pair/correlated risk across shards, complicating portfolio Greeks and netting. Mitigation: align tenant books that need joint risk onto the same shard; run portfolio/IPV risk aggregation off the hot path as a separate fan-in.

Staleness vs throughput in surface fan-out: aggressive conflation lowers load but can serve a quote against a slightly stale surface during a fast move. Mitigation: bound and measure publish-to-snapshot lag, tag quotes with surface epoch, and tighten conflation on volatile pairs; never conflate the authoritative arb-free update used for booking.

Consensus on the hot path is a stealth latency killer: routing pricing/quoting through Raft would serialize on quorum and destroy tail latency. Mitigation: keep the cluster thin (Aeron guidance) — only durable, must-order lifecycle events go through consensus; pricing stays in-node and replayable from the log asynchronously.

DPDK/RDMA ops and licensing/portability cost: dedicated-core ownership, driver/NIC pinning, and no native f64-on-Metal-style portability gaps; premature adoption adds complexity without proven need. Mitigation: defer behind io_uring/SO_REUSEPORT, gate on measured bottleneck, document as ADR with OSS fallback first-class.

Fleet upgrade correctness: rolling shard-by-shard upgrades must preserve in-flight quotes/orders during handoff AND keep the partition map consistent so the router never sends to a draining shard's old process. Mitigation: versioned partition map + router-coordinated drain + standby coverage + N/N-1 wire compat gates already specified for the single-node handoff.

Determinism across the distributed layer: bit-identical reproducibility (a stated NFR) is harder once events are replicated/replayed across nodes and clocks differ. Mitigation: drive all pricing inputs from the ordered replicated log (single source of truth), seed RNG from log position, and reconcile via the existing f64 CPU oracle.
